motivation.why_the_exploratory_number_cannot_be_tru: The recombination assumes adaptive_rows = control_rows + new_only_rows is what a REAL sequential walk would produce. That assumption silently smuggles in an assumption that is FALSE in general: this engine holds exactly ONE position at a time (broker-verified-flat-before-entry, C11), and the raw signal population (334 entries, IDENTICAL regardless of min_contracts -- qty is not a run_backtest kwarg, confirmed by n_raw_entries=334 on both CONTROL and VARIANT in the parent study's own JSON) is generated WITHOUT knowledge of which entries will actually be affordable/taken. A qty=3 fallback trade that floor=5 could never afford may, under the adaptive rule, OCCUPY THE POSITION SLOT and be still open when a LATER signal arrives that floor=5-only CONTROL would have taken at qty=5 -- pre-empting it. The naive union counts BOTH trades' P&L unconditionally, which cannot happen in reality (the engine cannot hold two positions). This mechanism is invisible to any per-row recombination and only surfaces in a true entry-time-ordered, exit-time-gated sequential walk.
motivation.precedent_this_exact_artifact_already_bu: backtest/tools/filter5_ribbon_fate_2026_07_31.py's attribution_block(): a headline +$738.60 'from deleting filter 5' decomposed to 86% position-sequencing/pre-emption -- the gate's own added cohort was worth ~$4.93/trade, essentially the entire headline was control trades vanishing because an unlocked earlier entry consumed the single-position slot on the same day, not evidence the gate blocks money. That helper's own docstring states the decomposition exists 'so this can never be silently omitted again.' This study reproduces that decomposition for the adaptive-sizing case rather than assuming the recombination is exact (it is exact for PER-ROW P&L given a fixed admit/deny set -- proven true and reused below -- but NOT exact for WHICH rows end up admitted, which is exactly the gap a sequential walk closes).

hypothesis: A two-tier adaptive sizing rule (try qty=min_contracts_preferred=5 first; fall back to qty=min_contracts_floor=3 ONLY when 5 itself is RISK_CAP-unaffordable at the current premium/equity) captures a material share of floor-3's participation gain while preserving floor-5's runner-cohort edge (every floor-5-affordable trade keeps qty=5, unchanged from CONTROL) -- NET of whatever real position-sequencing losses the newly-admitted qty=3 fallback trades cause by occupying slots that would otherwise have gone to a later floor-5-affordable signal. The exploratory $+10,528.60 recombination is the CEILING on this hypothesis (zero sequencing loss); the true sequential-walk number is expected to be lower and may fall anywhere between CONTROL's $+7,448.40 and that ceiling, including possibly below CONTROL if pre-emption is severe (per the filter-5 precedent, this is a real, not hypothetical, risk).

This is evaluated on the SEQUENTIAL-REPLAYED set, never the naive union.
secondary_metrics: day-majority: NOVEL TERM, no repo precedent found (grep for day_majority/day-majority/majority_of_days/days_positive across the whole repo returns zero hits) -- defined FRESH here, frozen before running: group the sequential-replayed adaptive population's trades by entry calendar date (ET), sum P&L per day; classify each day as up (day_total > 0), down (day_total < 0), or neutral (day_total == 0, excluded from the ratio, reported separately). PASS iff up_days > down_days (strict majority among decided days).

method.tool: NEW backtest/tools/bold_adaptive_sizing_2026_08_02.py, built on top of backtest/tools/bold_fullhist_replay.py MINIMALLY extended (same additive-parameter pattern min_contracts already used 2026-08-02 for the parent study): (1) replay_population()'s row capture gains one new field, exit_time_et (currently computed by walk_exit_manager as WalkResult.exit_time_et but discarded -- only hold_minutes survives into the row dict), needed to determine when a position frees the single slot; (2) a new resolve_bold_qty_adaptive(entry_premium, equity, per_trade_risk_cap_pct, min_contracts_preferred=5, min_contracts_floor=3) sibling to the existing resolve_bold_qty, tries preferred first (same notional<=cap check), falls back to floor, else None; (3) replay_population() gains a qty_mode: str = 'fixed' parameter ('fixed' = byte-identical existing behavior via min_contracts/resolve_bold_qty; 'adaptive' = uses resolve_bold_qty_adaptive and ignores min_contracts). Every existing call site omits qty_mode and is therefore byte-identical (parity guard required, mirrors the parent study's own TestToolExtensionParity pattern).
method.why_no_new_backtest_walk_is_needed_for_p: walk_exit_manager's decision core (automation/state/fleet/exit_manager.py#plan_exit_actions) evaluates TP1/runner/stop/trail thresholds as PERCENTAGES of entry premium or absolute chart levels -- never as a function of open_qty's absolute size -- and the ExitState.from_entry leg split (int(qty*tp1_qty_fraction) / qty-tp1_qty) is verified non-zero at both qty=3 and qty=5 (task step 4, re-verified fresh in this study's own guard file, not just cited from the parent). Therefore exit TIMING (exit_time_et, exit_reason, hold_minutes) for a GIVEN entry is identical whether walked at qty=3 or qty=5; only dollar_pnl (and the per-leg $ split) scales with qty, with the already-documented sub-linear-at-qty3/super-linear-at-qty5 TP1-split wrinkle (bold_fullhist_replay.py's run_first_consumer_elite_bull_delta docstring). This means the EXISTING CONTROL (min_contracts=5) and VARIANT (min_contracts=3) replay_population() outputs already contain every per-row P&L number this study needs -- the parent lane's per-row math was correct; only the ADMISSION SET (which rows actually get taken, in what order, given ONE shared position slot) was never verified. This study adds exactly that missing sequential-admission pass, reusing (not re-deriving) the per-row P&L.
